text.p: Time Warner Inc. said Wednesday it will sell its stake in American Lawyer Media, a publisher of legal magazines and newspapers, and Counsel Connect, an online service for lawyers, as part of its previously announced plan to sell non-core assets.

The media and entertainment giant also said it would keep its interest in Court TV and said American Lawyer Media founder and Chief Executive Steven Brill, who had led a group that sought to acquire both Court TV and American Lawyer Media, will resign from American Lawyer Media in six months.
Time Warner said it was selling American Lawyer Media and Counsel Connect to reduce debt.
The company said Brill sold his share of the American Lawyer Media and Court TV partnerships to Time Warner after the company decided to retain its interest in Court TV.
Court TV, a partnership of Time Warner, NBC and Liberty Media Corp., was launched in July 1991, and now has 30 million subscribers.
American Lawyer Media, which owns the flagship American Lawyer Magazine, has the highest average-subscriber income of any paid-circulation magazine in the world, Time Warner said.
